# Recorded comparison on the Jammertest 2024 data

> RECORDED: receiver output of the Jammertest 2024 campaign (Andoya, Norway), controlled jamming, spoofing and meaconing. One u-blox receiver. Not from the Gulf and not from a robot. Evidence kind: recorded. Session level labels only.

Generated from `sim/results_r3/recorded/` by `docsgen/facts.py`. The design, detectors, split and criteria were fixed in `docs/ANALYSIS_PLAN_R3_RECORDED.md` and frozen by hash (`data/r3_recorded/PLAN_FREEZE.json`) before the scorer was run. The scorer was run once (state: run once). Nothing was tuned afterwards.

## What was run

24 recordings, 12 used for calibration and 12 held out. The monitor under test (M) is the round one and two code, unchanged. Four baselines read the same data: D-RX (receiver flags), D-JAM (the receiver jamming indicator against a threshold of 45.00 set on calibration recordings), D-JUMP (position jump against receiver velocity) and D-NIS (a constant velocity Kalman filter with a chi square gate). The odometry stream that M needs is the receiver velocity held at ten hertz, not a wheel encoder.

## Reading

M raised 47.60 false alarms per nominal hour on the recordings (interval 32.56 to 67.20), against 0.30 on the synthetic arm built from the developer's parameters. It alarmed in 19 of 24 sessions and for 39 of 40 loss of fix events. At its own nominal rate, M would be expected to alarm 29.12 times per session by chance, so session detection alone is weak evidence for M. Of the baselines, D-JAM had the lowest false alarm rate.

Limits. One campaign in Norway, one receiver type, no Gulf data and no robot. Labels are session spans, so a missed session may be a session in which the attack had no effect on the receiver. The odometry substitute is derived from the same receiver, so the monitor never sees an independent motion estimate, which is the situation it was designed for; the false alarm result therefore shows how M behaves with this substitute and does not show how it would behave on a robot with wheel odometry. Dust, glare and heat have no recorded counterpart and remain synthetic.
